question: What was one of the negative impacts of the Green Revolution? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Soil degradation due to excessive use of fertilisers
Increased reliance on traditional seeds
Reduced yields in staple crops
Increase in organic farming
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Soil degradation due to excessive use of fertilisers

Explanation:
The Green Revolution significantly increased food production but had negative impacts. Excessive use of chemical fertilisers led to soil degradation, reducing land fertility and increasing environmental pollution. Additionally, High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds required more water and pesticides, straining water resources. Long-term use of chemical fertilisers deteriorated soil structure and caused micronutrient deficiencies. Thus, soil degradation was a major negative impact of the Green Revolution.

☛ Main objective of the Green Revolution → Increase food grain production
☛ Crops most associated with HYV seeds → Wheat and rice
☛ Environmental impact of the Green Revolution → Soil and water pollution
☛ Start of the Green Revolution in India → 1960s
question_hi: हरित क्रांति के नकारात्मक प्रभावों में से एक क्या था? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: अत्यधिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग से मृदा क्षरण

मुख्य फसलों में उपज में कमी

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अत्यधिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग से मृदा क्षरण

Explanation:
हरित क्रांति ने खाद्य उत्पादन बढ़ाया, लेकिन इसके नकारात्मक प्रभाव भी हुए। अत्यधिक रासायनिक उर्वरकों के उपयोग से मृदा क्षरण हुआ, जिससे भूमि की उर्वरता घटी और पर्यावरण प्रदूषण बढ़ा। इसके अलावा, उच्च उपज वाली किस्मों (HYV) के बीजों के लिए अधिक पानी और कीटनाशकों की आवश्यकता ने जल संसाधनों पर दबाव डाला। रासायनिक उर्वरकों के लंबे समय तक उपयोग से मिट्टी की संरचना खराब हुई और सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्वों की कमी हो गई। इस प्रकार, मृदा क्षरण हरित क्रांति का एक गंभीर नकारात्मक प्रभाव था।

question: What is the southernmost point of the Indian mainland called today? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Indira Point
Nicobar Islands
Cape Comorin
Kanyakumari
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kanyakumari

Explanation:
The southernmost point of the Indian mainland is Kanyakumari, formerly known as Cape Comorin. It is located in the state of Tamil Nadu and is the meeting point of the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean. This place is famous for its spectacular sunrise and sunset views over the ocean. Note that the southernmost point of India is Indira Point in the Great Nicobar Islands, but that is not part of the mainland. Hence, the correct answer for the mainland's southernmost point is Kanyakumari.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is the southernmost point of India? → Indira Point (Great Nicobar Island)
☛ What is the southernmost point of the Indian mainland? → Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin)
☛ In which state is Kanyakumari located? → Tamil Nadu
☛ Which water bodies meet at Kanyakumari? → Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean
☛ Where is the Vivekananda Rock Memorial situated? → Kanyakumari
question_hi: भारतीय मुख्य भूमि के सबसे दक्षिणी बिंदु को आज क्या कहा जाता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: इंदिरा पॉइंट
निकोबार द्वीप समूह
केप कोमोरिन
कन्याकुमारी
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है कन्याकुमारी

Explanation:
भारतीय मुख्य भूमि का सबसे दक्षिणी बिंदु कन्याकुमारी है, जिसे पहले केप कोमोरिन कहा जाता था। यह तमिलनाडु राज्य में स्थित है, जहाँ अरब सागर, बंगाल की खाड़ी और हिंद महासागर का संगम होता है। यह स्थान अपने सूर्योदय और सूर्यास्त के दृश्यों के लिए प्रसिद्ध है। ध्यान रखें कि भारत का सबसे दक्षिणी बिंदु इंदिरा पॉइंट (ग्रेट निकोबार द्वीप) है, जो मुख्य भूमि का नहीं बल्कि द्वीपीय क्षेत्र का हिस्सा है। इसलिए मुख्य भूमि का सबसे दक्षिणी बिंदु कन्याकुमारी है।

question: Identify the group of crops which is grown in Kharif Season in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Groundnut and Barley
Gram and Mustard
Urad and Cotton
Jute and Wheat
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Urad and Cotton

Explanation:
In India, Kharif crops are sown during the monsoon season (June-July) and harvested in October-November. Both Urad (black gram) and Cotton are Kharif crops. Urad is a leguminous pulse crop that requires warm and humid climate, while Cotton is a cash crop grown in the Kharif season. Among other options: Groundnut is Kharif but Barley is Rabi; Gram and Mustard are Rabi crops; Jute is Kharif but Wheat is Rabi. Hence, only Option 3 has both crops as Kharif.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Major crops sown in Kharif season → Rice, Maize, Cotton, Groundnut, Urad, Jute
☛ Major crops sown in Rabi season → Wheat, Barley, Gram, Mustard, Peas
☛ Sowing time of Kharif crops → June-July (with onset of monsoon)
☛ Scientific name of Cotton → Gossypium hirsutum
☛ Urad is a pulse crop rich in protein → Grown in Kharif season
question_hi: भारत में खरीफ के मौसम में उगाई जाने वाली फसलों का समूह पहचानें? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: मूंगफली और जौ
चना और सरसों
उड़द और कपास
जूट और गेहूँ
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है उड़द और कपास

Explanation:
भारत में खरीफ फसलें मानसून के मौसम (जून-जुलाई) में बोई जाती हैं और अक्टूबर-नवंबर में काटी जाती हैं। उड़द और कपास दोनों खरीफ फसलें हैं। उड़द एक दलहन फसल है जो गर्म और नम जलवायु में उगाई जाती है, जबकि कपास एक नकदी फसल है जिसे खरीफ मौसम में बोया जाता है। अन्य विकल्पों में, मूंगफली खरीफ है पर जौ रबी फसल है; चना और सरसों रबी फसलें हैं; जूट खरीफ है पर गेहूँ रबी फसल है। इस प्रकार, केवल विकल्प 3 में दोनों फसलें खरीफ हैं।

question: What separates the North Andaman and South Andaman islands? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Coco Channel
Ten Degree Channel
Palk Strait
Duncan Passage
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Duncan Passage

Explanation:
Duncan Passage separates the North Andaman and South Andaman islands. It is a 48 km wide waterway. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands is a union territory of India, located in the Bay of Bengal. The Ten Degree Channel lies between the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, while the Palk Strait separates India and Sri Lanka. The Coco Channel lies between Myanmar and the Andaman Islands. Duncan Passage is named after a British naval officer named Duncan. This question is important for understanding the geography of Indian islands and their separating channels.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which islands does Duncan Passage separate? → North Andaman and South Andaman
☛ Between which island groups is Ten Degree Channel? → Andaman and Nicobar Islands
☛ What does Palk Strait separate? → India and Sri Lanka
☛ Between which regions is Coco Channel? → Myanmar and Andaman Islands
☛ Width of Duncan Passage? → 48 km
question_hi: उत्तरी अंडमान और दक्षिणी अंडमान द्वीपों को कौन अलग करता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)

दस डिग्री चैनल
पाक जलडमरूमध्य
डंकन पैसेज
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है डंकन पैसेज

Explanation:
डंकन पैसेज उत्तरी अंडमान और दक्षिणी अंडमान द्वीपों को अलग करता है। यह 48 किलोमीटर चौड़ा जलमार्ग है। अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह भारत का केंद्र शासित प्रदेश है, जो बंगाल की खाड़ी में स्थित है। दस डिग्री चैनल अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीपों के बीच स्थित है, जबकि पाक जलडमरूमध्य भारत और श्रीलंका को अलग करता है। कोको चैनल म्यांमार और अंडमान द्वीपों के बीच स्थित है। डंकन पैसेज का नाम ब्रिटिश नौसेना अधिकारी डंकन के नाम पर रखा गया है। यह प्रश्न भारतीय भूगोल में द्वीपों के स्थान और जलडमरूमध्य को समझने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।

question: Which of the following island groups has the smallest land area? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Ritchie’s Archipelago
Nicobar Islands
Lakshadweep Islands
Andaman Islands
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lakshadweep Islands

Explanation:
Lakshadweep is the smallest Union Territory of India, with a total land area of only 32 sq km. It comprises 36 islands, of which 10 are inhabited. Comparatively, the Andaman Islands have an area of about 6,408 sq km, the Nicobar Islands about 1,841 sq km, and Ritchie’s Archipelago (part of Andaman) about 1,000 sq km. All these island groups fall under either the Andaman and Nicobar Islands or Lakshadweep. Lakshadweep is located in the Arabian Sea and is known for its coral reefs and marine life. Its administrative headquarters is Kavaratti.

☛ Total area of Andaman Islands → 6,408 sq km
☛ Area of Nicobar Islands → 1,841 sq km
☛ Number of islands in Lakshadweep → 36
☛ Administrative headquarters of Lakshadweep → Kavaratti

निकोबार द्वीप समूह
लक्षद्वीप
अंडमान द्वीप समूह

Explanation:
लक्षद्वीप भारत का सबसे छोटा केंद्र शासित प्रदेश है, जिसका कुल भूमि क्षेत्रफल केवल 32 वर्ग किमी है। इसमें 36 द्वीप शामिल हैं, जिनमें से 10 पर मानव बस्ती है। तुलनात्मक रूप से, अंडमान द्वीप समूह का क्षेत्रफल लगभग 6,408 वर्ग किमी है, निकोबार द्वीप समूह का लगभग 1,841 वर्ग किमी है, और रिची द्वीपसमूह (अंडमान का भाग) का क्षेत्रफल लगभग 1,000 वर्ग किमी है। ये सभी द्वीप समूह अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह या लक्षद्वीप के अंतर्गत आते हैं। लक्षद्वीप अरब सागर में स्थित है और अपने मूंगा चट्टानों और समुद्री जीवन के लिए प्रसिद्ध है। इसका प्रशासनिक मुख्यालय कवरत्ती है।

question: Which mountain range acts as a natural boundary between the Northern Plains and the Deccan Plateau? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Satpuras
Aravallis
Himalayas
Vindhyas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vindhyas

Explanation:
The Vindhyachal mountain range acts as a natural boundary between the Northern Plains and the Deccan Plateau. It stretches approximately 1,100 km in an east-west direction. The average elevation of the Vindhyas is about 300-600 meters. This range passes through the states of Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar. The Vindhyas have a mention in ancient Indian literature and are considered an important geographical divide of central India. The Satpura range lies to its south, the Aravallis to the northwest, and the Himalayas to the north.

☛ Average elevation of Vindhyas → 300-600 meters
☛ Vindhyas in ancient texts → mentioned in Mahabharata and Puranas
☛ Rivers flowing through Vindhyas → Narmada (south side), Tons, Ken
☛ Region between Vindhyas and Satpuras → Narmada Valley

question: What was the primary occupation of most of India’s population on the eve of independence? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Trade
Agriculture
Education
Industry
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Agriculture

Explanation:
At the time of independence, India was predominantly an agrarian economy. Over 85% of the population lived in villages and their primary occupation was agriculture and related activities. Industrial development was very limited, and most industries operated according to British interests. The level of education was also low, with only a small section being literate. Trade was mainly confined to the export of raw materials. Thus, agriculture was the backbone of the Indian economy before independence, providing employment to the majority of the population.

question_hi: स्वतंत्रता की पूर्व संध्या पर भारत की अधिकांश जनसंख्या का मुख्य व्यवसाय क्या था? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 2)

कृषि
शिक्षा
उद्योग

Explanation:
स्वतंत्रता प्राप्ति के समय भारत एक कृषि प्रधान देश था। लगभग 85% से अधिक जनसंख्या गाँवों में निवास करती थी और उनका मुख्य व्यवसाय कृषि और उससे जुड़ी गतिविधियाँ थीं। औद्योगिक विकास अत्यंत सीमित था और अधिकांश उद्योग ब्रिटिश हितों के अनुरूप संचालित होते थे। शिक्षा का स्तर भी निम्न था और केवल एक छोटा वर्ग ही शिक्षित था। व्यापार मुख्यतः कच्चे माल के निर्यात तक सीमित था। इस प्रकार, स्वतंत्रता पूर्व भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था की रीढ़ कृषि ही थी, जो अधिकांश जनसंख्या को रोजगार प्रदान करती थी।

question: Which of the following crops was primarily associated with the Green Revolution in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Oil
Wheat
Pulses
Cotton
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Wheat

Explanation:
The Green Revolution in India occurred during the 1960-70s, led by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan. Its main objective was to increase food grain production, with wheat and rice being the primary crops. High-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, especially Mexican wheat varieties, were used. States like Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh saw a huge increase in wheat production. The Green Revolution made India self-sufficient in food grains. Dwarf wheat varieties with the Norin-10 gene doubled yields. Oil, pulses, and cotton were not the main focus of the Green Revolution.

question_hi: भारत में हरित क्रांति से मुख्य रूप से कौन सी फसल जुड़ी थी? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)

दालें
कपास

question: What type of rainfall occurs along the Western Ghats due to moist air being obstructed and forced to rise along the Ghats?  (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Cyclonic rainfall
Frontal rainfall
Convectional rainfall
Orographic rainfall
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Orographic rainfall

Explanation:
When moist air is obstructed by the Western Ghats and forced to rise, it leads to orographic rainfall. This type of rainfall occurs when moist winds encounter a mountain barrier, causing the air to ascend, cool, and condense, resulting in precipitation on the windward side. The Western Ghats experience heavy rainfall during the monsoon due to this mechanism, while the leeward side remains dry due to the rain shadow effect. Orographic rainfall is common in coastal regions of India, the Himalayas, and the northeastern states.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Cause of orographic rainfall → Moist air forced to rise over mountains
☛ Rain shadow area is formed → On the leeward side of the mountain
☛ Wettest place in India → Mawsynram (Meghalaya)
☛ Why eastern slope of Western Ghats gets less rain → Due to rain shadow effect
☛ Heavy rainfall in Mumbai is due to → Orographic effect of Western Ghats
question_hi: पश्चिमी घाट के साथ-साथ नम हवा के रुकावट और घाटों के साथ ऊपर उठने के कारण किस प्रकार की वर्षा होती है? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which pass in the Himalayas connects Himachal Pradesh with Ladakh?  (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Nathu La
Bum La

Baralacha La
solution:

It lies on the Manali-Leh Highway and is used for vehicular movement. The name Baralacha La means 'pass with four peaks'. The Chandra and Bhaga rivers originate near this pass. question_hi: हिमालय में कौन सा दर्रा हिमाचल प्रदेश को लद्दाख से जोड़ता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)

question: What was the major reason for the poor performance of the agriculture sector during the 1960s? (RPF Constable 2024 (06/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Frequent droughts and famines
Low investment in technology
Overdependence on imports
Lack of skilled labour
solution:

Explanation:
The poor performance of the agriculture sector in India during the 1960s was primarily due to frequent droughts and famines. The decade witnessed severe droughts in 1965-66 and 1966-67, causing a sharp decline in food grain production and forcing heavy dependence on food imports. At that time, irrigation facilities were limited and farmers relied on traditional methods. Although low investment in technology, overdependence on imports, and lack of skilled labor were present, natural calamities were the main cause.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the left-bank tributaries of Ganga river? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: Which of the following physiographic divisions of India is considered as ‘Tableland’? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: The Peninsular Plateau
The Coastal Plains
The Himalayan Mountains
The Great Indian Desert
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Peninsular Plateau

Explanation:
Among the physiographic divisions of India, the Peninsular Plateau is considered a 'Tableland' or plateau. It is the oldest landmass of India, formed from the ancient Gondwana Land. The plateau is bounded by the Vindhya and Satpura ranges in the north, and the Western and Eastern Ghats in the south. Its average elevation ranges from 600 to 900 meters. The Peninsular Plateau is divided into three parts: the Central Highlands, the Deccan Plateau, and the Northeastern Mountain Ranges. This region is rich in mineral resources and is drained by major rivers like Narmada, Tapti, Godavari, and Krishna.

question: In the Indian tradition, which of the following is NOT one of the six two-monthly seasons? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Pravara
Vasanta
Hemant
Sharada
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pravara

Explanation:
In Indian tradition, there are six seasons: Vasanta (Spring), Grishma (Summer), Varsha (Monsoon), Sharada (Autumn), Hemanta (Pre-winter), and Shishira (Winter). These seasons last two months each and divide the year according to the Hindu calendar. Pravara is not one of the six recognized seasons. Vasanta occurs in March-April, Grishma in May-June, Varsha in July-August, Sharada in September-October, Hemanta in November-December, and Shishira in January-February. This classification is mentioned in ancient Indian texts like the Vedas and Puranas.

question: The Satpura Range is a part of the Peninsular Plateau and is located between which two rivers? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Narmada and Mahi
Krishna and Kaveri
Godavari and Krishna
Narmada and Tapi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Narmada and Tapi

Explanation:
The Satpura Range is a major part of the Peninsular Plateau in central India. It runs in an east-west direction and is located south of the Narmada River and north of the Tapi River. Both the Narmada and Tapi rivers flow westward and empty into the Arabian Sea. The Satpura Range is a remnant of ancient fold mountains, running parallel to the Vindhya Range. This region is rich in biodiversity and houses the Satpura National Park. The range acts as an important link connecting the Vindhyas and the Sahyadri (Western Ghats).

question: Tropical rainforests are mainly NOT found in which of the following regions? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Western slope of the Western Ghats

Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
Andaman and Nicobar Islands
solution:

Explanation:
Tropical rainforests are found in hot and humid regions with high rainfall. In India, they are mainly located on the western slopes of the Western Ghats, the north-eastern states (like Assam and Meghalaya), and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar primarily have tropical dry deciduous or monsoon forests, not rainforests. These states receive relatively less rainfall and experience greater temperature variation, which is unsuitable for rainforest growth.
